articles.title: Not Their First Rodeo: MIT Study Finds 14% of Merging Black Holes Are Second-Generation
articles.summary: A new MIT analysis of 155 black hole mergers suggests about 14% are second-generation — born from previous black hole collisions, not dying stars. These cosmic “repeaters” spin much faster, offering a new window into how black holes grow in dense stellar environments.

articles.title: Cretin Family: Billie Joe Armstrong Leads All-Star Ramones Tribute Supergroup
articles.summary: Punk royalty unite: Green Day’s Billie Joe Armstrong, Rancid’s Tim Armstrong, Blink-182’s Travis Barker, and Ramones bassist C.J. Ramone form Cretin Family for a one-night-only 50th-anniversary Ramones tribute at Hollywood Forever Cemetery on August 30. Proceeds benefit cancer research.

articles.title: Carcinization Strikes Again: New Study Traces the Crab Shape’s Repeated Evolution
articles.summary: The crab body plan is so successful that evolution keeps reinventing it — a phenomenon called carcinization. A new preprint reveals that sideways walking likely evolved once in true crabs, but the broad, flat form appeared independently multiple times in anomurans like king crabs and hermit crabs.
